# DPI scaling on Windows

@difference Programs on Windows are DPI aware: Windows does not scale their windows, so one pixel of the program is one pixel of the screen at any scaling.

The original programs have no manifest, so Windows treats them as not aware of the DPI and stretches their window by the scaling of the display (150 % makes an 800x600 window cover 1200x900 physical pixels and look blurry). `blitzcc` embeds an application manifest in every program it builds for Windows that declares per monitor DPI awareness (version 2), support for long paths and the Windows versions 7 to 11. The window of `Graphics` is therefore as many pixels large as asked for, the mouse coordinates are pixels of the window, and `GraphicsWidth`, `GraphicsHeight` and the display modes are physical pixels.

The manifest is a resource that `blitzcc` writes next to the program while linking; no resource compiler is needed. A program built with `--llvm-flag` that names a `.res` file or a manifest (`-Wl,/manifestinput:...`) keeps its own and does not get this one. For MinGW targets the linker `lld` is used, because the GNU linker does not take resource files.
